comment: Open-source, free, ONNX-based neural TTS models. Artifacts are downloaded from official public releases (k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx 'tts-models' and 'vocoder-models' releases; rhasspy piper converted models; hexgrad Kokoro; Coqui VITS ONNX exports). Each piper artifact is a self-contained tar.bz2 with model.onnx, tokens.txt and espeak-ng-data. Kokoro artifacts contain model.onnx, tokens.txt, voices.bin (multi-lang adds espeak-ng-data + lexicon-*.txt). Matcha needs the shared vocoder vocos-22khz-univ.onnx (kind=file in shared_artifacts). MMS (vits) needs the shared espeak-ng-data tarball. Coqui (vits) models are character-based (model + tokens only; frontend=char, no espeak-ng or lexicon).

tts.name: Piper
tts.voice_cloning_note: Upload a converted Piper voice model (tar.bz2) or a model.onnx + tokens.txt pair trained from your own voice.

variants.name: Version 0.19 (English only, 11 voices)
variants.note: This artifact contains 11 English speakers only (sids 0-10); use the multilingual version below for Hindi, French, Chinese and other languages.

variants.name: Version 1.0 (53 voices - ALL languages: English, Hindi, French, Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Portuguese)
variants.note: The full multilingual Kokoro model. Contains every language voice in one download: American/British English, Hindi (Alpha, Beta, Omega, Psi), French, Chinese, Japanese, Italian and Portuguese. Bundles espeak-ng-data and lexicon-*.txt; all lexicon files are passed to the engine automatically.

variants.name: Version 1.0 int8 - ALL languages (quantized, ~62% smaller)
variants.note: Same 53 multilingual voices as Version 1.0 (English, Hindi, French, Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Portuguese) but int8-quantized: lighter download and faster on CPU.

variants.name: Version 1.1 (103 speakers, Chinese + a few English)
variants.note: Kokoro v1.1-zh (hexgrad/Kokoro-82M-v1.1-zh): 103 speakers, mostly Chinese with 3 English voices. Use Version 1.0 for Hindi, French, Japanese, Italian and Portuguese.

variants.name: Version 1.1 int8 (quantized, ~62% smaller)
variants.note: Same 103 speakers as Version 1.1 (mostly Chinese + 3 English) but int8-quantized: lighter download and faster on CPU.

tts.name: VITS zh-AISHELL3
tts.note: Multi-speaker VITS model (174 speakers, 8 kHz) trained on the AISHELL-3 dataset. The voice list shows one entry; the default speaker (sid 0) is used.

tts.name: Matcha-TTS
tts.license: CC-BY-4.0 (icefall conversion); LJSpeech/other datasets may have their own terms
tts.note: Matcha-TTS uses a separate neural vocoder (vocos-22khz-univ.onnx, ~51 MB) which is downloaded once and shared by every Matcha voice.

tts.name: OmniVoice
tts.voice_cloning_note: OmniVoice supports zero-shot voice cloning from 3-15 seconds of reference audio, plus voice design from text descriptions. Requires NVIDIA GPU and the omnivoice-triton package (pip install omnivoice-triton).

variants.name: Hybrid mode (~3.4x faster, may leak VRAM)
variants.note: WARNING: Hybrid mode has a known VRAM leak bug. Memory grows per request until OOM. Use triton mode for production.

tts.name: OmniVoice Server
tts.voice_cloning_note: OmniVoice Server provides an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API for TTS with voice design, cloning, streaming, and concurrent requests. Other apps on the same network can also use it. Requires NVIDIA GPU and the omnivoice-server package.

variants.name: Server mode (OpenAI-compatible HTTP API)
variants.note: Runs as an HTTP server. Other apps on the network can use it too.

voices.name: Alloy (female, young adult, moderate pitch, american accent)
Echo (male, young adult, moderate pitch, american accent)
Fable (male, middle-aged, low pitch, british accent)
Nova (female, young adult, high pitch, american accent)
Shimmer (female, young adult, moderate pitch, australian accent)

variants.name: Server mode - Voice Clone (use reference audio)
variants.note: Clone any voice from 3-15 seconds of reference audio.
